advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile record_comment_id's "never remapped" docstring with the code (either guard against remapping to a different id, or correct the docstring).
evidence: binding_store.py:495-506 docstring: "Append-only and idempotent: an identical re-record is a no-op ...; a key is never remapped to a different id."

Code: `if comment_ids.get(key) == str(jira_comment_id): return` then `comment_ids[key] = str(jira_comment_id)` — a key already mapped to a DIFFERENT id is silently overwritten rather than rejected/no-op'd.
advisory.finding: BindingStore.record_comment_id's docstring states "a key is never remapped to a different id", but the implementation unconditionally overwrites an existing key when the new id differs — the only early-return is for an identical re-record.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either return early (or raise/log) when comment_ids.get(key) is set and differs, or change the docstring to say the last write wins.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the differ's secondary compare-key fit use the same fit function the Cloud send path applies (codec.fit_outbound) so near-limit bodies compare identically.
evidence: adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py:515-516 `codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body))`; rich_text_codec.py:46-54 fit_outbound uses adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit / fit_markdown_to_adf_limit (serialized-ADF measure)
This only bites when the PRIMARY comment_ids map write was lost (crash between add_comment and record_comment_id), which is exactly the case the secondary skip exists to cover.
advisory.finding: The demoted SECONDARY body-equality skip fits its compare key via sanitizer.fit_comment (plaintext char truncation, comment_limits.truncate_comment_body), while the Cloud send path (acli add_comment) fits the body via codec.fit_outbound (serialized-ADF-length measure). For a near-limit comment these two truncations can differ, so the landed Jira body will not equal compare_body and the secondary skip fails to suppress a re-post.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Evaluate whether record_comment_id must save() per comment, or whether the write-ahead durability goal can be met with a single flush at the end of the comment loop.
evidence: binding_store.py:503 `self.save()` inside record_comment_id, invoked per add_comment at both enactment sites (dispatch_apply_phases.py:377, dispatch_one.py:384)
binding_store.py:282-297 save() json.dumps the whole self._data and os.replace()s the whole file each call
advisory.finding: BindingStore.record_comment_id calls self.save() (a full-file JSON serialize + atomic tempfile replace of the entire bindings.json) on every recorded comment id; a create/update that posts N new comments therefore performs N full-file rewrites in one pass.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that drives `_apply_outbound_update` with a `binding_store` kwarg and asserts it is forwarded into `update_one` (e.g. captured by the fake update_one, or an end-to-end assertion that the comment ID is recorded on this path).
evidence: test_outbound_update_combined.py:180 `applier._apply_outbound_update(mutation, client=client)` — no binding_store kwarg passed, no forwarding asserted

test_leaves_effect_matrix.py:182 `def fake_update_one(batch, cl, comment_errors=None, binding_store=None):` captures only `batch`/`client`; the driver never asserts the received binding_store nor drives _apply_outbound_update with one
ABSENCE: test_comment_id_capture.py exercises _update_one_dispatch_comments and create_one directly, bypassing the _apply_outbound_update -> update_one seam this diff changed
advisory.finding: The new binding_store forwarding on the typed-dispatch update path (apply_outbound._apply_outbound_update: update_one(..., binding_store=_kwargs.get("binding_store"))) has no test. No test passes a binding_store into _apply_outbound_update and asserts it reaches update_one, so a regression that dropped the _kwargs.get forwarding — silently failing to record the comment-ID map on this path — would not be caught.
scenarios: A future refactor drops or mis-keys `_kwargs.get("binding_store")`, so typed-dispatch outbound updates stop recording comment IDs and re-post comments on the next pass (the DIG-5301 duplicate class this story closes).
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_leaves_effect_matrix.py's outbound-update driver, invoke the handler with binding_store=<sentinel> and assert captured["binding_store"] is <sentinel>; or add a dedicated test in test_outbound_update_combined.py driving _apply_outbound_update with a real BindingStore and asserting comment_id_for(key) is recorded.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acli add_comment test with the cutover flag set to a cloud-including value asserting the --body reflects the rich-rendered ADF (rich=True branch).
evidence: test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py:47-71: both tests call add_comment with no cutover flag set, so rich resolves to False only
ABSENCE: no test sets REBAR_RECONCILER_RICH_TEXT_CUTOVER to a cloud-including value and asserts the acli --body reflects the rich-rendered ADF
advisory.finding: The acli comment ADF-encode path claims rendering is governed by cutover_clients() (AdfCodec(rich="cloud" in cutover_clients())), but both tests only exercise the default flag state (off -> rich=False). The rich=True branch (flag on) — a distinct rendering behavior the docstring asserts is flag-governed — is not exercised in the acli send test.
scenarios: Story 3388 cutover flips on for cloud; a bug in the rich=True acli encode path (rendering/serialization) ships uncaught because the acli test never exercises that branch.
